content: Venture capitalist Martin Casado discusses AI value distribution with hosts Theo Jaffee and Sophia Dew. He argues AI uniquely lets small teams deploy massive capital efficiently, making this technology cycle different from previous waves. Casado examines whether frontier labs will dominate or if open-source models, specialists, and applications will capture increasing value. Topics include model routing, AI economics, and founder-market fit. He suggests this may represent the greatest wealth creation opportunity since the 1990s.

Launching August 6, it sold nearly 100,000 copies day one and ~300,000 in its first week, earning ~$6 million with 96% positive reviews. The team leveraged millennial nostalgia for Y2K-era electronics and repair-video culture, building around validated core gameplay rather than betting on untested ideas.

title: 越会用 AI 的人，学习能力退化得越快
content: A study of 26,811 Chinese middle and high school students over 30 months found that AI use improved homework scores by 18% and reduced completion time by 30%, but caused a 20% drop in closed-book exam performance. The negative effect, termed "generative AI learning penalty," worsened over time as students increasingly outsourced rather than used AI as a tutor. Similar patterns appeared in doctors, writers, and programmers: AI improved immediate output but degraded underlying skills when removed. The penalty is narrowing but not disappearing, raising concerns about diminishing critical thinking and independent problem-solving abilities across age groups.

title: 什么都没造卖了80亿
content: OpenRouter, a 90-person AI model routing platform, was acquired by Stripe for $8 billion within 82 days of being valued at $1.3 billion. It aggregates 400+ AI models through a single API, charging 5.5% per transaction with 71% gross margins and $140 million annualized revenue. The article contrasts this with illicit "relay stations" in China that exploit stolen accounts, swapped models, and malware injection—operations now targeted by regulators. Meanwhile, Silicon Intelligence, a loss-making but neutral compute provider, pursues a Hong Kong IPO at $774 million valuation. The core analysis frames trust as transparency multiplied by certainty, questioning whether OpenRouter's neutrality can survive under Stripe's ownership given regulatory and data retention pressures.

title: 一夜上热搜的影后，让人看见港女最硬核的一面
content: Hong Kong actress Michelle Wai won Best Actress at the Hundred Flowers Awards for her role in *The Last Dance*, becoming the first Hong Kong performer to achieve this honor. Unlike glamorous stars of cinema's golden age, Wai represents a resilient grassroots "career actress" archetype: she endured decades of minor roles, financial hardship, and earned numerous vocational licenses as backup plans while persistently pursuing acting. Her success reflects broader industry shifts—Hong Kong cinema now produces fewer megastars but cultivates skilled craftswomen whose gritty realism and survival-honed performances anchor authentically local films, though they still face limited mainstream commercial opportunities.
